headlines.title: AppLovin Shares Surge as Revenue Continues to Soar. Is It Too Late to Buy the Stock?
headlines.summary: AppLovin stock had been in the dumps, but this could be the start of a big rally.

headlines.title: Trade Desk Fell 3% While AppLovin Soared 31%. Here’s What Its November 9 Report Has to Prove
headlines.summary: Key TakeawaysAppLovin closed up 31% on Thursday after a record quarter and Magnite rose as much as 17%, while The Trade Desk fell 3% ahead of its own report on Monday, Nov. 9.

headlines.title: AppLovin Soars 44% in Two Days on Q3 Beat: “The Transition Is Still in Front of Us”
headlines.summary: Key TakeawaysAppLovin stock jumped 44% in two days after third-quarter revenue rose 55% and its fourth-quarter guide topped estimates. The slowdown this year’s selloff priced in hasn’t arrived, and the new ad models behind the beat are only partly rolled out.

headlines.title: AppLovin CEO Says the Business Can “Compound at Roughly 30%” a Year for the Long Term
headlines.summary: Key TakeawaysAppLovin’s third-quarter revenue rose 55% to $2. 18 billion, and CEO Adam Foroughi said the business can grow about 30% a year over the long term.

headlines.title: AppLovin Jumps 8% as Post-Earnings Rally Extends; Unity Climbs 7%, Trade Desk Dips
headlines.summary: AppLovin buyers keep piling in after a blowout quarter, yet the stock still sits far below where it started the year. Can a premium valuation survive the next test, and why are rivals Unity and Trade Desk heading in opposite directions?

description: AppLovin Corporation provides end-to-end artificial intelligence-powered advertising solutions for businesses in the United States and internationally. It operates through two segments, Advertising and Apps. The company offers Axon Ads Manager, a suite of marketing solutions that enables developers to automate, optimize, and manage marketing efforts; MAX, an in-app bidding technology that optimizes the value of a publisher's advertising inventory by running a real-time competitive auction; Adjust, a measurement and analytics marketing platform; and Wurl, a connected TV platform, which distributes streaming video for content companies, provides advertising and publishing solutions. It serves individuals, small and independent businesses, enterprises, advertisers and advertising networks, mobile app publishers, and indie studio developers. The company was incorporated in 2011 and is headquartered in Palo Alto, California.
